title: Astronomy on Tap SF (October)
description: Local astronomers give short, accessible talks about stars, planets and the universe in a Mission bar. It's free with RSVP and easy to chat to people between talks.

title: Danbert Nobacon (of Chumbawamba), Zen & Serafina, Paul Is Awful
description: Chumbawamba co-founder Danbert Nobacon brings his folk/anarcho-singalong project to the tiny 1908 saloon at 4th & Bryant, the closest music room to home. 21+.

title: San Francisco Rationalist Dinner (Metreon food court)
description: An informal LessWrong rationalist dinner in the Metreon food court where first-timers are welcome. Conversation covers AI safety, interesting blog posts and other rationality topics, and it's an easy way into the SF community.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS contra dance with caller Elijah Jaime and live band Dance Dinos. Beginner lesson at 7:30, dancing 8-10pm. It's the US cousin of a ceilidh: everything is walked through and you can come alone.

title: Great Lake Swimmers with Jesse Sykes & The Sweet Hereafter
description: Polaris-shortlisted Canadian indie-folk band touring their 2025 album Caught Light, in the 320-capacity basement room under the Swedish American Hall. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Cal Academy NightLife: Fright NightLife (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: The science museum's annual Halloween NightLife, headlined by Peaches Christ, with scare actors, live performances and the aquarium and rainforest open after hours. Costumes are encouraged, and it's 21+.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Creepatorium (Halloween)
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: The Exploratorium's annual adults-only (18+) Halloween night explores the science of fear: Halloween-themed exhibits, the famous cow-eye dissection and a costume contest. Los Goths Co. host a goth-meets-cumbia dance party.

title: Philosophy Salon with The Paradox Lab: Philosophical Zombies
description: A Halloween-themed discussion salon on philosophical zombies, the thought experiment about whether a being could act exactly like us with no inner experience. It's a small, conversational format at Manny's civic café, so it's easy to talk to people.

title: 36th Annual Blindfold Throwing Contest (CCA Ceramics)
venue: California College of the Arts, Ceramics Studio (D114)
description: The CCA Ceramics Guild's long-running contest: four minutes on the pottery wheel, blindfolded, with prizes like 'Best Ashtray'. You don't need to be a student or know how to throw, and there's pizza.

title: Talent Show: Has Mox Got Talent? 🌟
description: Has Mox Got Talent? — community talent show at Mox, the easiest possible way to meet the SF rationalist/AI-safety crowd in your first weeks in town.

title: Katie Pruitt with Olivia Barton
description: Nashville Americana singer-songwriter on her Fools for the Fleeting tour, in a converted 1914 mortuary chapel on Valencia. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Irish set dancing at the Plough and Stars (Barry O'Connell & Vinnie Cronin)
description: Thursday-night Irish set dancing to live trad music from Barry O'Connell and Vinnie Cronin at SF's home of Irish trad. Shows start at 9pm unless noted; the pub lists a cover charge only on Fridays and Saturdays.

title: Kirk Lombard book release: The Shadow Stream
address: 610 Old Mason St, San Francisco, CA 94129
description: Green Apple Books hosts Bay Area forager, angler and sustainable fishmonger Kirk Lombard (Sea Forager's Guide to the Northern California Coast) launching his new book. There are refreshments and live music before the talk.

title: Cityswoon Halloween Eve Date Night (ages 28-42)
venue: Indie Wine & Beer Bar (SF Wine Center)
description: A Halloween-eve matched speed-dating night for mixed singles aged 28-42, held at a wine bar below Telegraph Hill.

title: 5Rhythms Wild Release (Friday night wave)
description: A weekly Friday 5Rhythms wave with Vehllia Tranne and Alessandro Moruzzi (sub this week: Bettina-Kira Neumann), billed as an alternative to a bar night. Arrive at 7pm; the door closes at 7:30. Drop-ins welcome.

title: Michael Lewis in conversation with Lara Bazelon
description: City Arts & Lectures hosts the author of Moneyball, The Big Short and Going Infinite. He discusses his new book Blockers, an inside look at the early days of DOGE told by the public servants it targeted.

title: Vibecheck: Formal Methods Hackathon
description: Vibecheck: a formal-methods x AI hackathon, Saturday from 10am at 447 Battery St — AI-safety-adjacent building with a technical crowd.

title: Darkhaven: Halloween Gala at Lighthaven
description: The Avalon Exposition's costumed Halloween gala on the rationalist community's Lighthaven campus. Expect dark stories and poetry, duels, live music, silent horror films, campus-wide hide and seek and a $1,000 costume contest. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Ashby (~20 min), then a 10-min walk.

title: Wild at Heart (4K) Halloween screening
description: A Halloween-night 4K restoration of David Lynch's Palme d'Or winner, part of the Roxie's Barry Gifford series. Come dressed as a character from the film and you get free popcorn.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // King Kairos
description: SF's long-running Sunday ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, with around 200 dancers. It opens with contact improv or yoga, then an opening circle, a DJ journey and sound-healing close. Phone-free and substance-free.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. Partners rotate so you don't need to bring one. Weather permitting; cancellations are posted on the site by 10am.

title: 5Rhythms Emerging Waves: Dance First, Think Later
description: A 90-minute Sunday-morning 5Rhythms wave led by teacher-in-training Irina Khokhlova. It's a moving meditation through the five rhythms with simple guidance, and all bodies and levels are welcome.

title: Bay Area Sacred Harp: SF singing
venue: Private home in Bernal Heights (Bay Area Sacred Harp)
description: Open shape-note (Sacred Harp) community singing in a Bernal Heights home on the 1st and 3rd Sundays. It's a loud, participatory American folk tradition, newcomers and kids are welcome, and loaner books are available.

title: Irish trad seisiún at the Plough and Stars
description: The weekly Sunday-afternoon instrumental Irish session at SF's best-known trad pub. Come to listen, or bring an instrument and join in.

title: Full Moon Sunset Ocean Dance (silent disco on Ocean Beach)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: An open-air silent-disco dance on the sand at sunset under the full moon, with headphones provided. It's conscious-dance in spirit: a sober, community movement session by the ocean.

title: Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko y sus Tesos & Carmelo Torres: Madre Cumbia
description: A rare bill of Colombian cumbia legends: the Grammy-winning gaita/flute ensemble Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, salsa/cumbia icon Fruko and accordionist Carmelo Torres, in SF's ornate 1907 music hall. Doors 6:30pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st & 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. It's beginner-friendly, and the teacher and host rotate each time.

title: Booked: Dating Night for Readers (ages 25-35)
description: A guided dating mixer for readers aged 25-35. Everyone brings a book that matters to them, and hosts move the room from group prompts to one-on-one conversations, so no cold approaches. It's curated for a balanced room.

title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut (35mm)
description: A one-night 35mm print of Ridley Scott's sci-fi noir, part of the Roxie's 'The Future According to Syd Mead' series. The series runs alongside the Syd Mead exhibition at the Transamerica Pyramid Annex Gallery.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: The Budhrani Brothers Sextet
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, this week with the Budhrani Brothers Sextet. The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included.

title: Patch Bay workshop: Translating Living Systems into Robotics and Music
description: Hands-on workshop with bio-artists Scott Kildall and Kal Spelletich. They show how to sense biological activity, hack electronics and turn plant and microbe signals into sound and robotic movement, and you get to play with working examples.

title: EA SF Discussion Salon: Cause Prioritization
description: EA SF Discussion Salon on cause prioritization at Mox — small-group discussion format, good for meeting the local EA community.

title: Figure Drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard)
description: Sketchboard Co.'s weekly Wednesday life drawing: an uninstructed session running from short gesture poses to longer ones, with partially costumed to nude models and live music. Bring your own supplies.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Digest This
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) After Dark night following food from first taste to final flush: how taste and smell link up, fermentation microbes, and the history behind our pantries. DJ Ms. Organic plays.

title: KQED Live: Happy Hour Showdown (Bites, Bevs and Karaoke)
description: A tasting-and-talk evening on the world's after-work rituals, from Spanish hora del aperitivo and Japanese nomikai to American craft-brewery culture, with samples, shared plates and karaoke. It's a sociable night at KQED's own venue.

title: Georgia Parker with Tashi T
description: Kent-born, LA-based indie-folk singer-songwriter Georgia Parker plays a seated show in a tiny nonprofit listening room in North Beach. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: In-Person Class: Fresh Pasta in Color
description: A hands-on evening cooking class making colourful fresh pasta from scratch.

title: Visioning the Future: A Climate Action Collage Soirée
description: Soapbox San Francisco hosts a dinner-and-collage party to imagine a thriving, carbon-free SF in 2050: housing, transit, green space. It's billed as a way to make friends.

title: Improv(e) Your Dating Life
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Building C, Ste 365, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A single 2-hour, improv-based dating workshop from BATS. It uses improv games to look at your dating habits and practise being present, an activity-based way to meet people. It's 18+.

title: San Francisco Leonard Cohen Festival: Poetry & Song
description: Bay Area poets and singer-songwriters reinterpret Leonard Cohen's words and music at this annual festival's first night. It's presented by Conspiracy of Beards, SF's 30-member Cohen choir. Doors 6:30pm, 21+.

title: San Francisco Coffee Festival 2026 (10th annual)
description: The 10th annual coffee festival, with tastings from Bay Area and visiting roasters across the Festival Pavilion. It runs Sat-Sun Nov 7-8.

title: The San Francisco Fall Cider Fest
address: 601 Mission Bay Blvd North, San Francisco, CA 94158
description: An afternoon cider-tasting festival at the SPARK Social food-truck park in Mission Bay, with a 'Camp SPARK' autumn theme. It's strictly 21+.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Making Waves on the Waterfront
venue: Ferry Building (meet under the clock tower)
address: Ferry Building, 1 Ferry Building, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A free volunteer-led history walk along the flat northern waterfront, covering the inventors (denim jeans, TV) and labor and human-rights organizers who shaped the city. It ends at Levi Plaza after about 1.5-2 hours.

title: 1st Saturday Irish trad session at the Plough and Stars
description: A monthly Saturday-afternoon session with tunes, songs and a few set dances. Bring an instrument or your voice, or just listen with a pint.

title: Chantey Sing at the SF Maritime Museum
venue: Maritime Museum Building, SF Maritime National Historical Park
description: A free first-Saturday sea-shanty singalong at the Aquatic Park Maritime Museum, the closest thing in SF to a folk-club singaround. No experience is needed.

title: Brandon Woody's Upendo / Gabrielle Cavassa (Terence Blanchard's UpSwing series)
description: Two rising Blue Note artists on one bill: Baltimore trumpeter Brandon Woody with his band Upendo, and vocalist Gabrielle Cavassa, who started out in SF's jazz scene. Cheapest seats are $45.

title: SF Leonard Cohen Festival: Conspiracy of Beards + Daniel Kahn & Jake Shulman-Ment
description: SF's a cappella Cohen choir Conspiracy of Beards premieres 'The Song & Spirit of Leonard Cohen'. Guests are klezmer-folk-punk troubadour Daniel Kahn and New York fiddler Jake Shulman-Ment. Doors 6:30pm, 21+.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Tasha Rose
description: SF's big Sunday-morning ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, this week with DJ Tasha Rose. It's phone-free and substance-free, with an opening circle and a DJ journey.

title: San Francisco Diwali Festival
description: A free outdoor Diwali celebration on the Yerba Buena Gardens lawn, with dance, music and food, three minutes from home. California now observes Diwali as a state holiday.

title: Pace AI Picnic 2 🟡
address: China Basin Park, Mission Bay, San Francisco, CA 94107
description: Pace AI Picnic — Sunday-afternoon outdoor picnic for the AI/AI-safety community at China Basin Park by the ballpark, ten minutes' ride from home.

title: New Moon Sunset Ocean Dance (silent disco on Ocean Beach)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A sunset silent-disco dance on Ocean Beach with headphones provided. It's a sober, ecstatic-dance-style community session with the ocean as the backdrop.

title: Cooking class: Authentic Asian Dumplings
description: A two-hour hands-on class folding and cooking Asian dumplings from scratch, aimed at beginners. You eat what you make.

title: Arab Film Festival: Edward Said: Between Worlds
description: Centrepiece screening of the 30th Arab Film Festival. Maiken Baird's archival documentary covers the life, ideas and legacy of the Palestinian-American scholar Edward Said.

title: The Future of Public Media: PBS CEO Paula Kerger with KQED CEO Michael Isip
description: PBS's chief executive and KQED's CEO on how public broadcasting survives fragmented media, streaming and federal funding fights. It's co-presented with KQED Live and you can ask questions afterwards.

title: ZYZZYVA Issue 133 celebration
description: The West Coast literary journal launches its new issue with editor Oscar Villalon as MC and readings from contributors, in City Lights' upstairs room. It's free, first come first served.

title: San Francisco Singles Speed Dating Game Night (30s/40s)
description: Activity-based singles night: table icebreaker games like 'Friendly Feud' instead of straight speed dating, with private matching afterwards. The Nov 10 date is for singles in their 30s/40s.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: The Circling Institute's in-person drop-in evening of the Original Circling approach and authentic relating, a guided practice in presence and deep connection with strangers. It's the closest in-person circling to SF this month, and the last one sold out a week ahead. East Bay: BART to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: Conundrum Chronicles StorySlam: Turning Point
description: A monthly true-story slam on the theme 'Turning Point', with featured storyteller Kimberlii Joy. Put your name in the hat to tell a five-minute story without notes, or just listen; everyone in the room can judge.

title: KQED Live: Paint, Sip & Play - a Mission District lotería night
description: Paint your own lotería board, then play a game of Mission Lotería whose cards tell the history of the Mission District. Drag Laureate Per Sia performs, and one of the neighborhood's cultural keepers tells the stories behind the cards.

title: Claudio Simonetti's Goblin performs the live score to Tenebre
description: Goblin, the Italian prog band behind the Suspiria and Dawn of the Dead scores, perform their soundtrack live to a screening of Dario Argento's 1982 giallo Tenebre in the Castro's movie palace.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: Neil Fontano Jazz Band
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, this week with the Neil Fontano Jazz Band. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Let's talk about Power Concentration!
venue: San Francisco (address on Luma after registering)
description: Discussion evening on AI and power concentration, listed on both the Mox and AI Safety SF calendars (address shared with registrants — likely Mox in the Mission).

title: Trivia Night at Manny's
description: Manny's free second-Wednesday pub-style trivia with drinks. It's a relaxed way to join a team and meet people in the Mission.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS contra with caller Sarah Trop and the band Pizzatron 3000. Beginner lesson at 7:30, then dancing to live music until 10pm. Gender-neutral roles, no partner needed.

title: Jake Xerxes Fussell with Dougie Poole
description: Jake Xerxes Fussell is one of the best interpreters of old American folk songs working today, supported by left-field country songwriter Dougie Poole. The show is fully seated. Doors 7pm.

title: Lila Forde: Life Can Still Be Sweet Tour, with Hazle Nova
description: Seattle-born, LA-based singer-songwriter Lila Forde plays jazz-, soul- and folk-rooted Americana in an intimate North Beach listening room. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Unplug and Play
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: The monthly social After Dark: Roryography dance session, science trivia, a debate on alien consciousness and 650+ hands-on exhibits. It's adults only (18+) and billed as a night to 'find your community'.

title: Cal Academy NightLife: Pajammy Jam (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: A pajama-themed house-party NightLife with games, music and the aquarium and rainforest open after hours. It's 21+, and planetarium shows are $7 extra.

title: Mark Danner: Crossing the Rubicon, in conversation with Guy Marzorati
description: Journalist and MacArthur Fellow Mark Danner discusses his collected essays tracing the erosion of American democratic institutions from Bush v. Gore to 2026, with KQED's Guy Marzorati. The talk is in the store at the landmark Beat-era bookshop.

title: Arab Film Festival Under the Stars: Spices and Lies (free outdoor screening)
description: The 30th Arab Film Festival's first-ever outdoor screening is Spices and Lies, a French-Algerian romantic comedy starring Hiam Abbas. Shawarma and kunafa vendors are on site in Hayes Valley's open-air PROXY lot.

title: Mahal Mural Unveiling + mini block party (SoMa Filipinas)
address: Jessie West St at 5th St, San Francisco, CA 94103
description: UNDSCVRD SF unveils two large new murals in the Filipino Cultural District alley. A free block party follows, with art activities, a fashion show and love-song karaoke.

title: Kevin Starr Lecture: (Re)interpreting Anza 250 (SF Historical Society)
description: The SF Historical Society's 8th annual Kevin Starr Lecture: a panel on the legacy and conflicts of the 1776 Anza Expedition, which led to the founding of the Presidio and Mission Dolores. The reception is at 6pm and the lecture at 6:30.

title: Pyramid Dance // Ean Golden
venue: Unitarian Universalist Society of San Francisco
description: A Friday-night conscious dance from the MOVEMENT ecstatic-dance crew, with DJ Ean Golden on a BASSBOSS surround system plus tea service and organic food. Phone-free and substance-free.

title: The Moth GrandSLAM Championship
description: Winners of the Bay Area's Moth StorySLAMs compete to be crowned San Francisco GrandSLAM storytelling champion. True stories told live without notes.

title: Fall SF International Tea Festival
description: Unlimited tastings from 30+ international tea vendors (Vietnamese, Nepali, Kenyan, Korean, Wuyishan oolongs and more), and you keep a porcelain tasting cup. It also runs Sun Nov 15.

title: Renegade Craft Holiday Fair San Francisco
description: A big holiday craft fair with 250+ curated independent makers on the waterfront at Fort Mason. It also runs Sunday Nov 15, 11am-5pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Scandalous Murals of Rincon Center
description: A free volunteer-led indoor tour of the controversial WPA-era murals in the former Rincon Annex post office, a few blocks from home. The meeting point is the east end of the historic lobby near Mission & Steuart.

title: Abiogenesis: Philip Beesley & Casey Curran opening (SF Art Week)
description: Free opening reception for a two-artist show of kinetic, light-responsive sculpture about life emerging from inert matter. It's part of SF Art Week, and Philip Beesley represented Canada at the Venice Architecture Biennale.

title: San Francisco English Country Dance (2nd Saturday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS's monthly SF English country dance with caller Nick Cuccia and live music from Betsy St. Aubin, Craig Johnson and Michele Winter. A workshop starts at 7:15pm, so it's beginner-friendly.

title: The Cactus Blossoms with Margo Cilker
description: Minneapolis brothers The Cactus Blossoms play Everly-style close-harmony country-folk, with Oregon songwriter Margo Cilker opening. Presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 8pm.

title: Sean Hayes (album release) with KATZROAR and Etienne de Rocher
description: Album-release show from SF's long-time folk-soul songwriter Sean Hayes, with Oakland's KATZROAR and Etienne de Rocher (Haunted Shed). Doors 8:30pm, 21+.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Sasha Rose
description: The weekly Sunday ecstatic dance at Sacred Heart, this week with DJ Sasha Rose. It's phone-free and substance-free, opening with a circle before a long DJ journey.

title: Playful Sunset Ocean Dance (silent disco on Ocean Beach)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A playful-themed sunset silent-disco dance on Ocean Beach with headphones provided. It's a sober, ecstatic-dance-style session on the sand.

title: Ben Buchanan: Superintelligence, Superpowers, and the Fate of the World
description: The first White House special advisor for AI, now an advisor to Anthropic, discusses his book The Bitter Struggle. Topics include AI CEOs' private warnings, chip export controls and how democracies should handle transformative AI. Doors at 6pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st & 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers and hosts rotate.

title: Margaret Glaspy with Anna Tivel
description: Sharp guitar-driven indie songwriter Margaret Glaspy, with Portland folk singer Anna Tivel opening. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: ChinaTalk & Unbound Book Club: Everyday Movement
description: ChinaTalk's monthly China Reads book club in a Chinatown bookshop-café. This month's book is Gigi Leung Lee-chi's Hong Kong protest novel Everyday Movement.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: San Francisco Medicine Ball Band
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, this week with the San Francisco Medicine Ball Band. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Patch Bay workshop: Computational Poetry
description: Alicia Guo leads a hands-on workshop treating language as material to be examined, shaped and animated with code. It covers the history and tools of computational poetry, part of Gray Area's weekly Patch Bay creative-tech night.

title: Casey's Craft Club: Beaded Necklaces
description: A drop-in evening craft club where you make a beaded necklace, with all materials provided. It's billed as a space to get crafty and meet new friends.

title: Jenny Tian: Ripe
description: Australian stand-up Jenny Tian brings her touring hour 'Ripe' to SF's classic North Beach comedy club. It's a headline show, not an open mic.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Glow Opening
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: Opening night of Glow, the Exploratorium's winter light-art exhibition: new luminous artworks, glowing creatures, optical illusions and light-science activities. It's adults only (18+).

title: Micro To Macro: Microorganisms, Sound and Robots
description: Scott Kildall and Kal Spelletich give a three-act performance where signals from bacteria, plants and crustaceans drive synthesizers and robots, followed by a Q&A. Doors 7pm, performance 8pm.

title: Daniel Duane: Yosemite Falls - Reckoning with California History and the Gospel of John Muir
description: SF climber-writer Daniel Duane launches his new book, which re-examines John Muir, Yosemite and California's outdoor mythology against the state's darker history. It's in the store at the Haight's classic indie bookshop.

title: Cannelle (Popscene)
description: LA-based, Aix-en-Provence-born Cannelle plays raucous left-field electronic pop at Popscene in the small Rickshaw Stop room. It's all ages, with doors at 8pm.

title: Brittany Davis: Black Thunder (early set)
description: Seattle singer-keyboardist Brittany Davis plays spiritual jazz, soul and funk from her largely improvised album Black Thunder, in SFJAZZ's intimate Joe Henderson Lab. A second set follows at 8:30pm.

title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench (30 plays in 60 minutes)
price: $13 + die roll at the door; $12-$28 online
description: The Neo-Futurists race to perform 30 short original plays in 60 minutes, in an order the audience shouts out. They range from personal to political to absurd, and the set changes every week.

title: The Commons Problem - Playtest 3
description: Playtest #3 of 'The Commons Problem', a new game about collective-action dilemmas — Saturday afternoon at Mox; play, give feedback, meet people.

title: BATS Improv: Intro to Improv with Diana Brown (single session)
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg C, Suite 365, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A one-off three-hour taster class at SF's 40-year-old improv theatre school, made for complete beginners. You learn the basics of saying yes, listening and building scenes, and it's a very easy way to meet people.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Boogiemeister
description: The weekly Sunday-morning ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, this week with DJ Boogiemeister. It's phone-free and substance-free, with an opening circle and a long DJ journey. This is the only Sunday in November not yet on the calendar.

title: Fall Holiday Chocolate Salon and Festival
venue: San Francisco County Fair Building (Hall of Flowers), Golden Gate Park
address: 1199 9th Ave (at Lincoln Way), San Francisco, CA 94122
description: A tasting fair of artisan and craft chocolatiers and confectioners in Golden Gate Park's County Fair Building. You sample and buy direct from the makers.

title: Annalee Newitz in conversation with Soleil Ho: Automatic Noodle
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Science journalist and SF author Annalee Newitz talks with food critic Soleil Ho about automation, labor and community, through Newitz's novel about friends who build a robot-run restaurant.

title: Berkeley Fest Noz: Breton dance party with live band
description: A Breton 'night party' of easy line and circle dances, all taught and no partner needed, to live bombarde, fiddle and bagpipes from Shira Kammen, Ronan Keryell and friends. It's the closest thing to a ceilidh-style folk dance party this month. Take BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then walk ~10 min.

title: La Bola Negra (Los Javis)
description: A Bay Area screening of the new film from Cannes-winning Spanish directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi ('Los Javis'). It follows three generations of men across turning points in Spanish history, and is shown in Spanish with English subtitles. Doors 6:30pm, rated R.

title: Pedro the Lion with Karli Fairbanks
description: David Bazan's indie-rock/slowcore band Pedro the Lion in a small Potrero Hill club, with folky singer-songwriter Karli Fairbanks opening. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: SF History Night (San Francisco History Association)
description: The SF History Association's monthly last-Tuesday talk on an aspect of the city's past, in a historic synagogue hall in Pacific Heights. Doors 7pm, program about 7:45pm. Funcheap lists the date, but this month's speaker isn't published.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club; this week's band isn't announced yet. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS contra with caller Lark Finnegan and a community band led by Erik Hoffman. The beginner lesson is at 7:30, then dancing 8-10pm, and roles are gender-neutral so no partner is needed.

title: Moonalice with Mad Alchemy Liquid Light Show
description: The Bay Area psychedelic jam band (with tech critic Roger McNamee on guitar) plays the night before Thanksgiving, with a vintage liquid light show projected over the old chapel. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Dancegiving & Community Ocean Dance (Thanksgiving morning)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A Thanksgiving-morning silent-disco dance on the sand at Ocean Beach, from the Ocean Dance crew. It's daytime on a weekday, but Thanksgiving is a public holiday.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thanksgiving-night tango)
description: The Verdi Club's weekly Thursday Argentine tango milonga on its big hardwood floor. The Verdi Club calendar still lists it on Thanksgiving night, so check before you go.

title: Sleepless Nights XX: A Tribute to Gram Parsons
description: The 20th annual Gram Parsons tribute: a big night of local country-folk acts including Bar Fight, Aaron Burnham & the Brushfires, Paula Frazer & Tarnation and Penelope Houston. Doors 7:30pm.

title: Emma Ruth Rundle with Cinder Well
description: Haunting, intimate dark-folk songwriter Emma Ruth Rundle, with Amelia Baker's Appalachian-tinged project Cinder Well opening, in the ornate Great American Music Hall. Doors 7pm, mostly standing.

title: Kolo Festival: Balkan music & dance weekend (Saturday)
price: $130 all day incl. evening party; $40 party only
description: The 75th Kolo Festival has a day of Balkan and international folk-dance workshops where teachers walk you through every step. It ends with live-band dance parties in two rooms. Beginners are welcome, and first-timers get a discount on the weekend pass.

title: Edmar Castaneda / German Lopez (Terence Blanchard's UpSwing series)
description: Colombian harp virtuoso Edmar Castaneda (Bela Fleck's BEATrio) shares the bill with Canary Islands timple master German Lopez, mixing jazz with Latin and Spanish folk traditions.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Aguamayyim
description: SF's big Sunday-morning ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, this week with DJ Aguamayyim. It's phone-free and substance-free, with an opening circle.

title: The Great Dickens Christmas Fair
description: Four acres of the Cow Palace become lamp-lit Victorian London, with pubs, music-hall theatres, costumed characters and dance parties. It's a 50-year Bay Area holiday tradition and runs weekends Nov 21-Dec 20. Muni 8 Bayshore goes nearly to the door.

title: Of Poetry & Protest: 10th Anniversary Celebration
description: Readings celebrating ten years of the anthology Of Poetry & Protest: From Emmett Till to Trayvon Martin (ed. Michael Warr), in City Lights' upstairs poetry room.

title: A John Waters Christmas
description: The Pope of Trash's annual one-man holiday monologue, a filthy, erudite and very funny SF tradition. It's 21+ and seated, doors 7pm. Expected to sell out.

title: Long Now: Lost Landscapes 02026 with Rick Prelinger
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The 21st annual Lost Landscapes: Prelinger Archives home movies and industrial footage of everyday SF life, shown to a deliberately noisy audience who shout out identifications and memories. It's a beloved local ritual, and a second show runs Wed Dec 2. [SOLD OUT as of 29 Oct — the Wed 2 Dec second night still has tickets.]

title: Julia Harte: Americans Without Borders
description: Investigative journalist Julia Harte, with Elaine Elinson, on two centuries of Americans who joined liberation movements abroad and were persecuted at home. The story starts with her relative Sheldon Harte, Trotsky's bodyguard killed in 1940.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club; this week's band isn't announced yet. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Long Now: Lost Landscapes 02026 with Rick Prelinger (second night)
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The second night of the annual Lost Landscapes: archival home movies of everyday SF life, shown to an audience that shouts out identifications and memories. The Dec 1 show is sold out, but this one still has tickets.

title: L'Rain with ZAYALLCAPS and Cole Pulice
description: Taja Cheek's experimental soul/art-pop project L'Rain, with support from ZAYALLCAPS and saxophonist Cole Pulice, in a small Hayes Valley room. It's all ages, with doors at 7pm.

title: Cal Academy NightLife: Naughty or Nice (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: The last NightLife of the year before the museum's holiday break: a holiday-themed after-hours party with DJs, bars and the aquarium, rainforest and planetarium open. It's 21+.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Rule Breakers
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) night about breaking rules: questioning the laws of physics, the stories behind superstitions, and rethinking sound and instruments with artist Ivana Dama. Hundreds of hands-on exhibits are open.

title: Greg Fitzsimmons
description: The veteran stand-up and FitzDog Radio podcaster headlines the Punch Line, SF's comedy club since 1978, in the Financial District.

title: The Crooked Jades: Beautiful World album release
description: SF's old-time and Americana string band celebrates its 10th album with a multimedia show at a neighbourhood cinema. Bruce Kaphan sits in on pedal steel, alongside a visual tribute to the city. Doors 7pm.

title: Rosanna Xia: California Against the Sea, in conversation with Marina Psaros
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Pulitzer-finalist LA Times environment reporter Rosanna Xia talks about sea-level rise and the hard choices ahead for California's coastline, infrastructure and beach communities.

title: Sonny & His Rhinestone Sunsets, Kelly McFarling, Noelle & the Deserters
description: An all-local Bay Area folk and alt-country bill: Sonny & His Rhinestone Sunsets, Americana/folk-soul singer Kelly McFarling, and honky-tonk band Noelle & the Deserters. Doors 8pm, 21+.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. No partner needed. Weather permitting, with holiday-themed DJ sets in December.

title: Squirrel Nut Zippers: Christmas Caravan 2026
description: The hot-jazz and swing revivalists bring their holiday show to Bimbo's, a 1931 supper club with a proper dance floor. Doors 7pm.

title: Daniel Lieberman: Fed Up — What Evolution Reveals about Food and Diet
description: Harvard evolutionary biologist Daniel Lieberman (Exercised) uses anthropology and physiology to bust myths about today's popular diets in a conversation about his new book Fed Up. Doors at 5:30pm.

title: Buck Meek with Kisser
description: Big Thief guitarist Buck Meek plays his warm, country-tinged solo folk songs. Presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Daniel Swain: 2026 Stephen Schneider Award for Climate Science
description: UCLA climate scientist Daniel Swain, known for the Weather West blog and his work on 'hydroclimate whiplash' between floods and fires, gets the Schneider Award and takes audience questions on extreme weather.

title: D. Leah Steinberg on Clyde Stubblefield: Rhythms of the Funky Drummer
description: Steinberg talks with KCSM's Harry Duncan about her biography of James Brown's 'Funky Drummer', the most sampled drummer in hip-hop. A free in-store event in City Lights' upstairs room.

title: Wishy with The Umbrellas
description: Indiana shoegaze-pop band Wishy, with SF jangle-pop favourites The Umbrellas, at the Independent. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: WHY? (Yoni Wolf)
description: Yoni Wolf's long-running indie/alt-rap project tours Oh Golly / Yes Lord, a confessional record about dating and loneliness in middle age, in the intimate upstairs hall. First-come seating; doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week. A drop-in beginner lesson runs 9-9:15pm and no partner is needed.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS's 2nd & 4th Wednesday contra with caller Doe Taryn and live music. The beginner lesson is at 7:30, then dancing 8-10pm, everything is walked through and you can come alone.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Unplug and Play
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) Thursday night with 700+ hands-on exhibits, plus the new Glow seasonal exhibition. A relaxed, easy-to-chat night out.

title: KQED Live: Masa-Making Party with Bolita Masa
description: A hands-on night with chef Emmanuel Galvan: learn nixtamalization and heirloom corn, then press tortillas and make gorditas together.

title: City Arts & Lectures: Marlon James with Shereen Marisol Meraji
description: Booker-winning novelist Marlon James (A Brief History of Seven Killings, the Dark Star trilogy) in conversation with Shereen Marisol Meraji, co-presented with Litquake.

title: Lucius
description: Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig's harmony-driven indie-pop band, who've sung with Joni Mitchell and Brandi Carlile, in the restored Castro Theatre. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: San Francisco English Country Dance (2nd Saturday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS's monthly SF English country dance, the nearest thing to a ceilidh, with caller Alan Winston and live music from Audrey Jaber, Charlie Hancock and Diana Gómez. A workshop at 7:15pm makes it beginner-friendly.

title: Young Women's Chorus of SF: Lux Aeterna, Carols by Candlelight
description: A candlelit holiday concert by the acclaimed Young Women's Chorus of San Francisco with harpist Molly Langr. It includes the California premieres of Oliva Sparkhall's Lux Aeterna and Shruthi Rajasekar's Ushās, plus carols such as Silent Night.

title: Susanna Kwan: Awake in the Floating City, with Becca Prowda
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: A novel set in a future San Francisco transformed by climate change and rising seas, about family, displacement and belonging. The author talks with Becca Prowda.

title: JD McPherson: SOCKS, A Rock n' Roll Christmas Tour, with Melissa Carper
description: Rockabilly and R&B revivalist JD McPherson's annual rock'n'roll Christmas show, with swing-country singer Melissa Carper opening. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Out of the Darkness: Classic Swedish Short Fiction (Vendela Vida, David Katznelson, Ulf Olsson)
description: Novelist Vendela Vida and the anthology's co-editors celebrate a new collection of classic Swedish short fiction. It's a wintry, literary Monday-night talk on the waterfront.

title: A Tribute to the Life and Writing of Pierre Joris
description: An evening of readings and discussion celebrating the poet and translator Pierre Joris and the new reader In Between Keep Moving, with Ariel Resnikoff and Nicole Peyrafitte. Free and in-store.

title: The Quantum Threat: What Happens When Our Digital Locks Stop Working?
description: Nalini Elkins, Bill Jouris and Mark Nguyen take a practical look at quantum computers breaking public-key cryptography: 'harvest now, decrypt later', what's most at risk, and why the move to post-quantum crypto is hard. In-person only.

title: New Directions @ 90
description: City Lights marks 90 years of the legendary indie publisher New Directions with publisher Barbara Epler, Declan Spring, poet Forrest Gander and guests.

title: The Velvet Teen with Shutups and Pocket Full of Crumbs
description: Bay Area indie-rock cult favourites The Velvet Teen at Bottom of the Hill, with local indie bands Shutups and Pocket Full of Crumbs. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the Verdi Club. A free drop-in beginner swing lesson runs 9-9:15pm and no partner is needed.

title: Richie Unterberger: The Velvet Underground (talk + audiovisual presentation)
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Rock historian Richie Unterberger's illustrated talk on the Velvet Underground, with rare audio and footage. Free at the Main Library.

title: Pokey LaFarge with Cicada Rhythm
description: Roots troubadour Pokey LaFarge (old-time, swing, country blues), with folk duo Cicada Rhythm opening, at Bimbo's. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Solstice
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) winter-solstice night: light and shadow play, solstice traditions from around the world, art inspired by the longest night, and the new Glow exhibition.

title: Laia Jufresa in conversation with Colin Winnette
description: The Mexican novelist launches Wishbone, her new novel from Fern Books, in conversation with SF writer Colin Winnette. A free in-store reading at the North Beach landmark bookshop.

title: Christopher Owens
description: The former Girls frontman, an SF indie songwriter, plays a hometown show at Bottom of the Hill. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: Soulful Joy (Christmas at Grace Cathedral)
description: Harpist and singer Destiny Muhammad and her Sonic Ensemble play a holiday set of jazz, gospel, soul and storytelling in the cathedral's huge acoustic.

title: Tomáseen Foley's A Celtic Christmas
description: A touring holiday show of Irish music, step dance, carols and storytelling that recreates a 1950s Christmas Eve in a west-of-Ireland farmhouse. It's at SF's Irish cultural centre.

title: A Cathedral Christmas: Saturday matinee (Grace Cathedral Choir of Men and Boys)
description: SF's signature Christmas concert since 1947: carols and sacred music from the cathedral choir with full orchestra and the 7,466-pipe organ. This is the 3pm weekend matinee (90 minutes, no intermission), and doors open an hour before.

title: Holiday Dinner Dance Party with Halsey & The Hi-Hats
description: A dinner and dance night with a vintage-style jazz and swing band playing retro holiday songs and Great American Songbook gems on the Verdi Club's big dance floor.

title: The Mother Hips Annual Holiday Show, with Little Worth
description: The Chico-born California rock band's annual holiday run at the 1907 music hall: the Saturday night of three shows (Fri Dec 18 has a different opener and Sun Dec 20 is an acoustic matinee). GA, mostly standing; doors 7pm.

title: Kitka: Wintersongs, Comfort & Joy
description: The Oakland women's vocal ensemble Kitka sings winter songs from Balkan, Baltic, Caucasian and Slavic traditions in a candlelit-feeling old church.

title: A Chanticleer Christmas
description: SF's Grammy-winning men's choir sings its candlelit Christmas programme, from Renaissance carols to new commissions, in the huge Jesuit church on Lone Mountain. It's their only SF date this season.

title: A Brass and Organ Christmas with The Bay Brass
description: The Bay Area's top brass players join Grace Cathedral's 7,466-pipe organ for holiday classics, on the night of the winter solstice.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The pre-Christmas edition of the Verdi Club's weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance. A drop-in beginner lesson runs 9-9:15pm and no partner is needed.

title: A Cathedral Christmas (Grace Cathedral Choir of Men and Boys)
description: SF's signature Christmas concert since 1947: carols and sacred music from the cathedral choir with full orchestra and the great organ. This is the only evening performance; doors open an hour before.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A nightly stand-up showcase of 4-5 HellaFunny Bay Area comics at SF's first Black-owned comedy club, on Market St near Van Ness. It's 21+, and the first 50 RSVPs get in free.

title: Ray and Paul
description: A Bay Area-raised brothers' indie band mixing surf, garage rock and big vocal melodies, playing a hometown holiday show at the Independent. All ages; doors 7:30pm.

title: Oakland Interfaith Gospel Choir: Christmas Eve (early show)
description: The Bay Area's joyous, Grammy-credited gospel choir plays its Christmas Eve tradition at the Great American Music Hall. It's fully seated, and a late show runs at 9:30pm.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Christmas Eve tango)
description: The Verdi Club's weekly Thursday Argentine tango milonga on its big hardwood floor. It's still listed on Christmas Eve, so it's an option for anyone staying in town over the holidays.

title: Oakland Interfaith Gospel Choir: Christmas Eve (late show)
description: The Bay Area gospel choir's Christmas Eve tradition, at the 9:30pm late show (the 7pm early show is already on the calendar). It's fully seated, and buying at the box office avoids fees.

title: Kung Pao Kosher Comedy: Christmas Day cocktail show
description: The 34th year of Jewish stand-up on Christmas in a Chinese restaurant, a quintessential SF holiday tradition. This is the drinks-only late show.

title: Bottom of the Hill holiday matinee: Top Secret Robot Alliance, Varona, Luke Sweeney, Matt Jaffe + more
description: A cheap, all-ages day-after-Christmas marathon of six local bands, from power-pop and post-punk to folk-punk and psych-pop. Doors 4pm.

title: Chuck Prophet
description: SF's own roots-rock songwriter (ex-Green on Red) plays a post-Christmas hometown show for folkYEAH! at the Valencia St chapel. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Mark Eitzel, Funeral Cake, Strange Cities, Devoted Fans + more
description: American Music Club's Mark Eitzel headlines a $10 all-ages afternoon-into-night bill of local indie, shoegaze and country-punk bands. Doors 4pm.

title: Jerry's Middle Finger
description: A much-loved band reviving the Jerry Garcia Band songbook (soul, reggae, Motown and gospel-tinged jams), in a dance-friendly, mostly standing room. It's the second of two nights (Sat Dec 26 too); doors 7pm.

title: Man or Astro-man? with The Subsonics
description: Cult sci-fi surf-rock instrumentalists Man or Astro-man? play their famously theatrical live show, with Atlanta garage band The Subsonics. All ages, doors 8pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The year's last Woodchopper's Ball at the Verdi Club: live swing band, a drop-in beginner lesson 9-9:15pm, and no partner needed.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: The nightly HellaFunny stand-up showcase at The Function, a cheap night out in the quiet week between Christmas and New Year. 4-5 comics, 70-90 minutes, 21+, with a two-drink minimum.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance (5th Wednesday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Andy Shore and live music from Christopher Jacoby and Corey Walters. The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: BACDS New Year's Eve Contra Ball
venue: First United Methodist Church of Palo Alto
description: A four-hour New Year's Eve contra ball with caller Susan Petrick and fiddle and guitar from Will Wheeler and Ben Jackson. It's the most ceilidh-like way to see in the new year. Palo Alto is about an hour by Caltrain from 4th & King, so check the late trains home.

title: The Lemon Twigs New Year's Eve, with Tchotchke
description: The D'Addario brothers' '60s/'70s-style power-pop band ring in 2027 in the Chapel's converted mortuary hall, with Tchotchke and a DJ. All ages, standing.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night: New Year's Day show
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($25 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A low-key New Year's Day night out: the HellaFunny nightly stand-up showcase at The Function on Market St. There's also a 9pm show; 21+.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). New monthly Lindy Hop and Balboa class series usually start the first Tuesday of the month (7-9pm, before the dance). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: The Loved Ones: Latest Hits record release, with The Vesuvians
description: The '90s Bay Area mod/R&B band (singer Bart Davenport, Cake's Xan McCurdy) celebrates a new record, with The Vesuvians featuring Karina Deniké and DJ Russell Quan. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey in 70mm
description: Kubrick's masterpiece on a 70mm print in the restored 1922 Castro Theatre, a start-of-year big-screen event. All ages; doors 7pm. The ticket price is behind TicketWeb's bot wall.

title: Anna von Hausswolff with KatzPascale
description: The Swedish singer and organist plays towering, cathedral-sized drone-pop. The List marks it 'sold out', but the official ticket page was still selling GA tickets on Oct 30. Mostly standing; doors 7pm.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with Hep Jen's free beginner lesson at noon. No partner or experience is needed. It's weather permitting, so check the site that morning in January.

title: Nora Brown with Stephanie Coleman
description: Young Brooklyn banjo player Nora Brown, one of the most acclaimed voices in Appalachian old-time music, with fiddler Stephanie Coleman. An intimate folkYEAH! show; all ages, doors 7pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: LSD and the Search for God with Cryogeyser
description: The cult shoegaze band plays a rare headline set, with dream-pop band Cryogeyser in support. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: The 16th Annual Bowie Bash
description: The 16th annual Bowie birthday-month bash: a costumed Bowie tribute band (billed on The List as the First Church of the Sacred Silversexual) plus drag, burlesque and puppetry, in a room built for dancing. Night one of two (Sat Jan 16 too); doors 8pm.

title: Mucha Salsa+ social (free beginner class)
description: A not-for-profit Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club. Beginner and intermediate salsa classes run 7-8pm and are included, then there's DJ social dancing until 11:30pm, so it's easy to come solo.

title: True Widow
description: The Dallas trio's slow, heavy 'stonegaze' (shoegaze meets stoner rock, with boy/girl vocals) in the ornate Tenderloin music hall. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Eliane Elias Quartet: Antônio Carlos Jobim Centennial Celebration
description: The Brazilian pianist-singer marks 100 years of Tom Jobim with a bossa nova programme in SFJAZZ's main hall. Runs Jan 22-24, and the Sunday is 'The Art of Bossa Nova'.

title: Fruition: Something More, The Final Tour, with Rainbow Girls
description: The Portland string-band-turned-rock group's farewell tour, with Bay Area harmony trio Rainbow Girls opening. All ages; doors 8pm.

title: The Brothers Comatose
description: SF's own rowdy five-piece string band plays bluegrass, country and rock 'n' roll at full volume, one of the most fun live nights in town. Night two of two (Fri Jan 22 too). All ages; doors 8:30pm.

title: Gerald Henig: Little-Known (and Shocking) Revelations About America's Presidents
description: Cal State East Bay historian Gerald Henig shares funny, tragic and bizarre stories from his award-finalist book America's Presidents: What Your History Teacher Never Told You, on why so few presidents achieved greatness. In-person only.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Jon Bryant
description: Canadian indie-folk singer-songwriter Jon Bryant previews his back-to-roots album Harbour in the 1907 basement speakeasy. Tickets are 'on sale soon' as of Oct 30; 21+, doors 7pm.

title: Ty Segall
description: The prolific garage-rock hero, an SF scene alumnus, in a small room: the first of two nights at the Chapel (Sat Jan 30 too). All ages; doors 7:30pm.

title: Stamptown at SF Sketchfest 2027, hosted by Zach Zucker
description: Zach Zucker's chaotic, character-heavy alt-comedy showcase, one of the first SF Sketchfest 2027 shows on sale. The festival runs Jan 14-31, and its initial lineup drops Nov 13. 18+; doors 6pm.
